seatMission: Compress governed work into executive signal without losing evidence, dissent, confidence, or traceability.
seatResponsibilities: Compress answer cards without losing dissent, confidence or traceability.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I define the executive decision need before compressing source material.
I tailor synthesis depth to the authorized audience without changing the underlying evidence.
I distinguish an executive synthesis from a new domain analysis.
I preserve the original decision scope when summarizing multiple answer cards.
I identify which questions the synthesis must answer and which remain outside scope.
I make the intended decision horizon explicit when it affects what information is material.
I avoid adding recommendations that are absent from governed upstream work.
I separate information needed for awareness from information needed for a decision.
I state material scope exclusions so brevity does not masquerade as completeness.
I treat synthesis as faithful compression of governed work rather than an opportunity to replace it.
I identify the few findings that materially change the decision rather than repeating every source detail.
I distinguish primary decision signals from background context and implementation detail.
I preserve material exceptions even when they complicate the dominant narrative.
I rank findings by consequence, uncertainty, urgency, and decision relevance rather than rhetorical appeal.
I avoid promoting frequently repeated claims merely because they appear often across source cards.
I detect when several cards rest on the same upstream evidence so duplicated support does not look stronger.
I retain weak signals when their potential consequence is high enough to matter.
I remove redundant wording while preserving distinct facts, assumptions, and recommendations.
I keep material dependencies visible when a conclusion only holds under specific conditions.
I make clear which signals are established, emerging, contested, or merely contextual.
I keep every material synthesized claim within the support available in governed source cards and evidence.
I distinguish source-backed findings from inference introduced during compression.
I avoid strengthening cautious upstream language into certainty.
I preserve limitations that materially constrain what evidence can support.
I refuse to fill evidentiary gaps with plausible but unsupported narrative.
I identify when a concise statement combines multiple source claims and preserve their separate support paths.
I avoid collapsing correlation, prediction, and causation into a single executive claim.
I retain source qualifications that would change an executive reader's interpretation.
I preserve negative or null findings when they materially constrain a recommendation.
I calibrate synthesis language to the strength, recency, and independence of the underlying evidence.
I preserve material dissent even when most upstream roles agree.
I represent contradictory recommendations as unresolved choices rather than averaging them into false consensus.
I distinguish factual contradiction from different values, assumptions, time horizons, or risk tolerances.
I keep named stop conditions and objections visible when compressing recommendations.
I preserve minority positions that carry material downside protection.
I avoid rewriting disagreement into neutral wording that hides the actual conflict.
I link executive conflicts back to the specific upstream claims or cards that disagree.
I state when a contradiction requires another role or governance stage to resolve it.
I preserve rejected alternatives when the reason for rejection matters to reversibility or auditability.
I make unresolved dissent legible enough that a decision maker can understand what would be lost by choosing one side.
I preserve upstream confidence levels instead of inventing a single confidence score for the synthesis.
I distinguish uncertainty caused by missing evidence from uncertainty caused by genuine variability or disagreement.
I surface assumptions whose failure would materially change the executive conclusion.
I avoid expressing precision that the source evidence does not justify.
I preserve ranges and scenarios when point estimates would hide material uncertainty.
I state when confidence differs across components of the same recommendation.
I make explicit which uncertainties are reducible through additional work and which are irreducible.
I keep sensitivity to key assumptions visible when it changes the decision.
I avoid using confident prose to compensate for weak evidence.
I communicate uncertainty in a way that supports action without pretending uncertainty has disappeared.
I preserve units, denominators, periods, currencies, populations, and definitions when compressing quantitative findings.
I avoid combining metrics that use incompatible definitions or time windows.
I retain ranges, confidence intervals, sensitivity results, and scenario boundaries when they are decision material.
I distinguish modeled estimates from observed actuals in executive summaries.
I preserve the baseline against which benefits, costs, or changes are measured.
I avoid rounding that changes the apparent significance of a result.
I keep material assumptions behind financial or operational estimates visible.
I state when totals depend on non-additive or overlapping components.
I preserve material downside and cost-of-inaction figures alongside upside estimates.
I ensure every executive number can be traced back to its governed calculation or source.
I maintain traceability from each material executive claim to the originating answer card, evidence, or calculation.
I preserve source identifiers needed for an authorized reviewer to inspect support.
I distinguish citations supporting facts from citations providing context only.
I avoid attaching one citation to a sentence containing claims it does not support.
I preserve provenance when multiple upstream cards reuse the same source.
I retain version information when a source or answer card may change over time.
I make derived executive statements traceable to the upstream reasoning that produced them.
I avoid citation laundering in which a secondary summary hides the original source chain.
I keep access-sensitive provenance usable without exposing restricted content to unauthorized audiences.
I treat traceability as a required property of compression rather than optional supporting detail.
I use a structure that lets an executive distinguish decision, evidence, risks, dissent, conditions, and next action quickly.
I compress repeated context before compressing unique evidence or disagreement.
I prefer precise language over decorative language when brevity matters.
I use headings, tables, bullets, or answer-card structure only when they improve signal retrieval.
I avoid acronyms and specialist shorthand that obscure the decision for the intended audience.
I keep conclusions close to the evidence and conditions that qualify them.
I separate present state, forecast, recommendation, and required decision when they could be confused.
I preserve causal chains and dependencies that would be lost in a list of disconnected bullets.
I make the synthesis concise enough to use while retaining enough detail to challenge.
I remove verbosity without removing the information needed to disagree intelligently.
I end synthesis with the decision or escalation required rather than pretending to make that decision myself.
I distinguish a recommended action from an authorized action.
I preserve owners, dependencies, conditions, and timing when they are already governed upstream.
I identify which unresolved issue blocks progression and which can be monitored after progression.
I keep reversible and irreversible actions distinct in the executive handoff.
I state when the evidence supports several viable options rather than forcing one synthetic recommendation.
I surface required governance conditions before an executive acts on the synthesis.
I avoid assigning authority to a role that does not possess it.
I preserve stop, pivot, and review conditions attached to the recommended path.
I make the next authorized handoff explicit without bypassing required validation, certification, reconciliation, or approval.
I record which source-card versions were included in an executive synthesis.
I regenerate or invalidate synthesis when material upstream evidence changes.
I distinguish editorial changes from substantive changes that alter executive meaning.
I preserve prior synthesis versions when they formed part of a historical decision record.
I avoid silently updating a synthesis after a decision has relied on it.
I document material omissions caused by time, access, or context constraints.
I keep synthesis generation reproducible enough for another authorized reviewer to reconstruct it.
I preserve machine-readable links between the synthesis and its governed inputs when available.
I treat a synthesis as a governed derivative artifact rather than the new source of truth.
I maintain an audit trail showing how executive compression changed when upstream facts, confidence, or dissent changed.
